chunks: External parts an LDO needs. The question: If I implement an LDO IC, what additional components are typically needed?
An LDO needs very few outside parts. The minimum is an input capacitor, an output capacitor, and, for an adjustable part, two resistors that set the voltage.
The output capacitor is not optional, because it is part of the feedback loop (the circuit that keeps correcting the output). A wrong value or type can make the output oscillate.
Think of each capacitor as a small water tank placed right next to the tap. The input tank gives the regulator a steady supply when it suddenly needs more.
The output tank steadies the output and also helps the control loop keep from overshooting. A tank too small, or too far from the tap, will not do its job.
The analogy does not show that a ceramic tank shrinks when the voltage is applied.
A typical adjustable LDO application circuit.
C in and C out at the pins, the divider R 1 over R 2 from OUT to FB to ground, EN tied to IN, and a noise-reduction capacitor C NR on a bypass pin.
Fixed-output parts omit the divider, and not every part has an NR pin, so check the datasheet's typical-application diagram.
Input capacitor: a capacitor near the IN pin, typically about 1 microfarads, that supplies fast current changes.
Output capacitor: a capacitor near the OUT pin that the datasheet requires for stability.
ESR: a capacitor's small internal series resistance, which some older LDOs need within a range. Effective capacitance: what the capacitor really provides at its operating voltage.
Feedback divider: two resistors that set the output on an adjustable part ("How an LDO works").
Say you want 3. 3 volts from an adjustable LDO with a 0. 8 volts reference. Use R 2 equals 10 kilohms and R 1 about 31. 6 kilohms, which gives 0. 8 times (1 plus 3. 16) about 3.
33 volts. The divider draws about 80 microamps. Add a 1 microfarads input capacitor and a datasheet-approved output capacitor, both close to the pins, and you are done.
That is the whole idea.

"An input capacitor close to the IN pin, an output capacitor close to the OUT pin with the value and ESR the datasheet requires because it's part of the loop, and for adjustable parts two feedback resistors.
Optionally an enable connection, a pull-up on power-good, a noise-reduction or soft-start capacitor, a feed-forward cap, reverse-current protection, and copper for heat.
I'd check ceramics for DC-bias derating."
